mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown accelerating weekly declines (-40.9, -38.4, -48.1, -63.0), indicating compounding momentum in reduced retail and recreation activity. This downward momentum will persist into the next two weeks before any stabilization, keeping the forward 4-week mean below the trailing 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact: three consecutive weekly declines with accelerating magnitude
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds above its t-0w level within the next two weeks, reversing the observed acceleration trend.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility falls below a sustained threshold, it signals active policy-driven restrictions (reduced service, stay-home orders) that further suppress discretionary retail trips over the following four weeks, as fewer people can reach retail corridors via public transport.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -55 points from baseline
evidence_refs: fact: TRANSIT reached -59.6 at t-0w, below prior weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 4 weeks even though TRANSIT remains below -55 points.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous week-on-week increases in RESIDENTIAL and decreases in WORKPLACES indicate a coordinated behavioral shift toward staying home, which jointly reduces incidental and planned retail trips, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks beyond what either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises more than 1 point week-on-week while WORKPLACES falls more than 1 point week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact: RESIDENTIAL rose from 13.7 to 18.7 while WORKPLACES fell from -36.6 to -46.1 over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 4 weeks despite both conditions (RESIDENTIAL up, WORKPLACES down) holding jointly.

mechanism_narrative: As the pre-Thanksgiving and holiday shopping season approaches, essential and gift-related retail errands may partially offset recent declines in RETAIL_REC, especially if GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains stable, reflecting sustained necessity-driven trips that bleed into adjacent retail categories.
evidence_refs: fact: decision date is 2020-11-15, approaching US holiday shopping season
regime_hint: pre-holiday shopping season under tightening restrictions
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline through the next 4 weeks despite stable or improving GROCERY_PHARM readings.

mechanism_narrative: Large week-to-week swings in PARKS mobility reflect weather-driven reallocation of outdoor leisure time; when PARKS drops sharply, households substitute indoor retail and recreation visits in the following week, producing a short-term uptick in RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact: PARKS swung from -3.6 to -12.0 to -1.6 to -7.7 across the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following a PARKS decline greater than 8 points.

mechanism_narrative: Continuous decline in WORKPLACES mobility reflects reduced commuting-linked incidental shopping trips; this steady downward trend will continue to drag down RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as fewer people pass by retail corridors during commutes.
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES declined monotonically from -36.6 to -46.1 over the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 4 weeks even as WORKPLACES continues its downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: Once RESIDENTIAL mobility plateaus at an elevated level for two consecutive weeks, households may experience behavioral saturation with at-home confinement, producing a mean-reverting rebound in RETAIL_REC as pent-up demand for errands and leisure trips is released.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds +18 points from baseline for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact: RESIDENTIAL reached 18.7 at t-0w, the highest in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues declining for two consecutive weeks even after RESIDENTIAL plateaus above +18 points.

mechanism_narrative: When essential-trip proxy GROCERY_PHARM remains stable while outdoor-leisure proxy PARKS declines, reflecting colder pre-holiday weather, households shift displaced outdoor leisure time into essential and retail errands, producing a modest rebound in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks despite recent declines.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays within plus or minus 3 points while PARKS declines more than 5 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact: GROCERY_PHARM stayed between -14.6 and -17.0 while PARKS fell sharply between weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next 4 weeks despite both the GROCERY_PHARM stability and PARKS decline conditions holding simultaneously.
